With all due respect to those mods (who I do not know anything about one way or the other), we all know the biggest problem with reddit is that a handful of powermods have a death grip on the default subreddits and SJWs have control of all the major news and political subreddits. We all know by now how they operate. They are patient. The ones they can't get outright, they plant a passable alt account in to get a mod position and then use a combination of redditrequest and admin chicanery to oust the top mod and fill the mod spots up with their buddies. And we all know they will patiently do the same thing here. And why wouldn't they? It's a system that's worked perfectly for them for years now.

Right now they don't take voat seriously because it's a start up. I'm sure Digg felt the same way 9 years ago. But the Exodus will continue and they will turn their eyes on voat eventually.

For this reason I propose that the major subverses be subject to mod term limits. Maybe subject to election or tribal counsel, a watchdog group, or a politburo. I'm not concerned how it's done, but I do not want to see voat rise up, only to fall to the same death trap that grips reddit.

At the very least, /v/news, /v/worldnews, and /v/politics should have term limits. One person essentially having ultimate control of the major sources of news and political commentary is a dangerous game. One we have already witnessed first hand failing miserably.

I have so far seen many great things here on voat, and I hope I continue to always see great things. I intend absolutely no disrespect to any current subverse mod, and I hope they can understand where I am coming from with this.

Thank you for your time and I hope this sparks some fruitful discussion.
